## Our data: life expectancy by country and year

```{r}
# Load the file once. Every chunk after this one starts from gapminder_wide
gapminder_wide <- read_csv(here("data", "gapminder_life_expectancy_wide.csv"))
```

Source: Gapminder. The table has 194 rows and 303 columns.

---

## One row per country, one column per year

```{r}
# Three Baltic countries and four of the 301 year columns
gapminder_wide |>
  filter(name %in% c("Estonia", "Latvia", "Lithuania")) |>
  select(name, `1990`, `2000`, `2010`, `2023`)
```

Column names that start with a digit need backticks.

## Why the plot has no x

The years are the names of 301 columns. `ggplot()` needs one column that holds the years.

*R for Data Science* (2e), chapter 5, gives three rules for tidy data:

1. Each variable is a column.
2. Each observation is a row.
3. Each value is a cell.

Here, `year` is a variable spread over 301 columns. The table breaks rule 1.

---

# 1. Wide to long {background-color="#1a5276" style="color: white;"}

**pivot_longer()**

---

## pivot_longer() takes three arguments

| Argument | Job |
|----------|-----|
| `cols` | The columns to stack |
| `names_to` | Name of the new column that receives the old column names |
| `values_to` | Name of the new column that receives the values |

---

## Create gapminder_long

```{r}
# Keep the columns we need, then stack the year columns
gapminder_long <- gapminder_wide |>
  filter(name %in% c("Estonia", "Latvia", "Lithuania")) |>
  select(name, `1950`:`2023`) |>
  pivot_longer(
    cols = `1950`:`2023`,
    names_to = "year",
    values_to = "life_exp"
  )

gapminder_long
```

3 countries and 74 years give 222 rows. `names_to = "year"` avoids the default name, `name`, which already exists in our table.

---

## The plot is empty

```{r}
#| message: true
gapminder_long |>
  ggplot(aes(x = year, y = life_exp, color = name)) +
  geom_line()
```

Let us look at the data.

---

## year is text

```{r}
gapminder_long |>
  glimpse()
```

`year` is `<chr>`. `pivot_longer()` took the year from a column name, and column names are text. `ggplot()` puts text on a discrete axis and does not connect the points.

---

## Your turn 3 {background-color="#d5e8d4"}

**Turn `year` into a whole number, then draw the line plot again.**

```{r}
#| eval: false
gapminder_long |>
  mutate(year = ___(year)) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = year, y = life_exp, color = name)) +
  geom_line()
```

Answer: the function is [YOUR ANSWER HERE].

---

## The fix: as.integer()

```{r}
# as.integer() turns "1990" into 1990
gapminder_long |>
  mutate(year = as.integer(year)) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = year, y = life_exp, color = name)) +
  geom_line()
```

---

## Rewrite gapminder_long with the fix

```{r}
# One pipeline: filter, select, pivot, change the type of year
gapminder_long <- gapminder_wide |>
  filter(name %in% c("Estonia", "Latvia", "Lithuania")) |>
  select(name, `1950`:`2023`) |>
  pivot_longer(
    cols = `1950`:`2023`,
    names_to = "year",
    values_to = "life_exp"
  ) |>
  mutate(year = as.integer(year))
```

```{r}
gapminder_long |>
  ggplot(aes(x = year, y = life_exp, color = name)) +
  geom_line() +
  labs(x = "Year", y = "Life expectancy (years)", color = NULL)
```

---

# 2. Long to wide {background-color="#1a5276" style="color: white;"}

**pivot_wider()**

---

## table2 is long

```{r}
# table2 comes with the tidyr package
table2
```

The column `type` holds the names of two variables: `cases` and `population`. Each country and year takes two rows.

---

## pivot_wider() takes two arguments

| Argument | Job |
|----------|-----|
| `names_from` | The column whose values become new column names |
| `values_from` | The column whose values fill the new columns |

```{r}
# One column for cases and one for population
table2 |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = type, values_from = count)
```

12 rows become 6 rows.

---

## Recap {.smaller}

| Task | Code |
|------|------|
| Wide to long | `pivot_longer(cols = , names_to = , values_to = )` |
| Long to wide | `pivot_wider(names_from = , values_from = )` |
| Text to whole number | `mutate(year = as.integer(year))` |
| Columns named with digits | Use backticks: `` `1990` `` |
